articles.title: Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival Prizes: ‘After Elena,’ Alfredo Castro, Lucía Puenzo and ‘La Bola Negra’ Win Big
articles.summary: Spain’s Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival, one of Europe’s foremost Latin American cinema platforms, prized two of the region’s cinema greats, awarding top prizes to Chilean actor Alfredo Castro and Argentine writer-director Lucía Puenzo on Saturday night.
body: Huelva’s prizes highlight the festival’s focus under director Manuel H. Martín on crossover films, often mixing genre-bending and social issues to surprising effect. Top winner “After Elena.” from Chile’s Shawn Garry, turns on mourning but is a comedy; Lucía Puenzo’s “Pepita, the Gunslinger” is a gangster movie but the gangster is a woman who battles corruption. “Funk,” which won Duda Santos best actress, is a musical but “revolutionary,” says director Aly Muritiba, in its centering “Black joy.”
The 2026 awards also may be the gayest in Huelva’s history, with nearly half going to LGBT movies in a year where Variety has asked whether the 2026-27 Oscars season is their gayest ever.

The double nods for the Shawn Garry directed “After Elena”(“Después de Elena”) also underscore what Huelva does best: Highlighting titles that deserve further recognition which in the case of Latin America includes most of its movies, given they are under-covered by the international media.

articles.title: John Turturro Says ‘I Still Consider Myself a Beginner’ as He Gets Marrakech Film Festival Tribute Award: ‘Every Job Is Like a First Love’
articles.summary: Though his career has spanned over four decades, John Turturro still feels like it’s just the beginning. The 69-year-old actor and filmmaker was honored with a tribute award at Marrakech Film Festival on Sunday night, where he was greeted with roaring applause as he mimed the iconic bowling moves…
body: “I am a very fortunate person to make a good living as an actor, sometimes as a writer, a director, doing something that I deeply love. To put all of yourself into what you do and give a piece of that away in your work is something that I learned from my parents,” Turturro said. “They taught me that a job well done defines who you are. Building a house, making a dress was done brick by brick, stitch by stitch.”
He called filmmaking the “magic and beauty of life” and “an offering that you hope others will receive with open hearts.”

“A great writer, Cesare Pavese, once said that the only great thing in life is to begin. And I still consider myself a beginner in many ways,” he concluded. “For me, when I do a job, every job is like a first love. And I consider this award an encouragement to continue to try.”

articles.title: ‘Hunger Games’ Lead Joseph Zada on Filming His Breakout Movie Role and ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’s’ Intense Stunts: ‘I Look Like a F—ing Action Star!’
articles.summary: When it comes to taking on the leading role in one of the most beloved film (and literary) franchises, sometimes you just have to jump right in. At least that was the case for Joseph Zada, whose first day on set of “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” was spent filming the opening cornucopia
body: There’s a certain amount of pressure that comes with stepping into such an iconic role, but Zada relished being thrown into the chaos. The first five weeks of filming were dedicated to shooting inside the arena — a “genius” scheduling choice, the 21-year-old actor tells Variety — because it let Zada fully immerse himself in the environment that would change Haymitch forever.

“It was really good for stepping into the character’s body, and I started mainly working by myself and living in my character by myself before I had to go on and work with veterans in this crazy cast,” Zada says, referring to the film’s star-studded ensemble that includes Glenn Close, Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons and Oscar winner Kieran Culkin. “I was able to just get on set and be confident and work with the younger actors first before I had to go into the bigger scenes and heavy dialogue.”

articles.title: 5 Best Performances In The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping, Ranked
articles.summary: From Joseph Zada's Haymitch Abernathy to Elle Fanning's Effie Trinket, here are the five best performances in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.
body: It's a stacked cast and it's legitimately tough to choose, but ultimately, I've picked five performers who build upon the previous movies and performances from storied actors who defined these roles originally... and do so beautifully.

Fanning, a recently minted Oscar and Emmy nominee for her sensational projects "Sentimental Value" and "Margo's Got Money Troubles," is unsurprisingly great during her unfortunately limited screen time, particularly her delivery of Effie's most memorable line from the novel ("I confess to having a moment!"). Honestly, there are so many prequels possible in the wider Hunger Games world, and if Suzanne Collins ever wanted to a deep dive on Effie's whole "deal" and give her her own story, I wouldn't hate that. But she'd need to convince Fanning to return to really make the movie sing.

articles.title: Why Wiress From The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Looks So Familiar
articles.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping introduces younger versions of characters from Catching Fire, and you might recognize the actor who plays Wiress.
body: This article contains spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping."

The original "Hunger Games" raised the stakes for Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) by establishing that tributes from their home, District 12, have only ever won the Hunger Games twice in 74 years. That means they only have one mentor, the alcoholic Haymitch Abernathy (Woody Harrelson), unlike other Districts' tributes that have two mentors each.

"Hunger Games" author Suzanne Collins told the story of the first District 12 victor in "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" — Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler), who won the 10th Hunger Games decades before Katniss was born and then vanished. Now, "Sunrise on the Reaping" tells how Haymitch won his own Hunger Games.

articles.title: SHEGLAM Opens the Wizards’ Vault With Its Third Harry Potter Makeup Collection
articles.summary: The set features playful, wearable essentials for eyes, lips and complexion, each inspired by a familiar corner of the wizarding world.
body: The Wizards’ Vault Full Collection Set ($110.79) gathers every new piece into one magical lineup. It’s the easiest way to own the full drop, and a gift-ready pick for the Potterhead on any list.
The Mischief Managed Eyeshadow Palette ($11.89) opens like the Marauder’s Map to reveal 12 pans of magical mattes and silky shimmers. Its fold-out design makes finding favorite shades easy.

The Sorting Hat Mystery Lip Oil ($7.19) is a blind box holding one of four House-inspired clear lip oils: Gryffindor, Slytherin, Ravenclaw, or Hufflepuff. Every one delivers glossy, non-sticky shine with moisturizing comfort (seen at right).
Prefer to brew a custom shade? The Herbology DIY Lip Gloss Kit ($14.19) offers a mix of shades and textures for creating a one-of-a-kind gloss potion.

articles.title: Robert Redford And Scarlett Johansson's '90s Disney Neo-Western Movie Is Worth Revisiting
articles.summary: A young Scarlett Johansson starred in this Disney-backed '90s neo-Western film opposite Robert Redford, who also directed the sensitive drama.
body: Nicholas Evans' "The Horse Whisperer" was a publishing phenomenon in 1995. The novel is about a young girl who's involved in a horseback riding accident that kills her best friend and their horse, leaving her and her own horse seriously injured. When she falls into a deep funk, her mother whisks her off to rural Montana. There, they try to heal her horse emotionally via a horse whisperer. And while she is married, the mother finds herself falling in love with the handsome, deeply sensitive animal shrink, something which, according to many critics, transformed the narrative into a shamelessly sentimental romance à la "The Bridges of Madison County."

"The Horse Whisperer" isn't quite on the level of the movie version of "The Bridges of Madison County" ( a lovely film that Clint Eastwood saved from production limbo ), but the screenplay credited to Eric Roth and Richard LaGravenese is nuanced in a way that maybe the novel isn't. And though it's not one of Redford's best movies, it's a strong piece of work that deserves more attention.

articles.title: Tom Jackson, Denver Broncos’ All-Pro Linebacker and ESPN Analyst, Dies at 75
articles.summary: He spent nearly 30 years with the network, often teaming with Chris Berman: “We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet.”
body: Tom Jackson, who parlayed a 14-season stint as a stalwart linebacker on the Denver Broncos’ famed “Orange Crush” defense into a long career as a popular football analyst on ESPN, has died. He was 75.
Jackson died Friday, his family told the network. No cause was announced.

Berman said on Sunday NFL Countdown that Jackson’s death was unexpected and that he had spoken with his best friend “at length” on Tuesday. “He was a vital 75,” he said. On Nov. 1, they spent time on the ESPN set after Jackson arrived for a surprise visit.

Added ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro, “He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans.”

articles.title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Slays $120M at Box Office as Franchise Heats Back Up
articles.summary: The sixth film in the Lionsgate series rebounded after 2023's 'The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes,' while freshly expanded 'I Play Rocky' and newcomer 'Elsinore' also came out swinging.
body: The Hunger Games franchise has been revived at the box office. Meanwhile, I Play Rocky demonstrated major strength as it expanded wide with a rare A+ CinemaScore, and Elsinore notched a promising per-screen average in limited release.

Lionsgate released The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping in 4,018 North American theaters, and the sixth film in the dystopian franchise grossed $120 million in its opening weekend. This gives it the fourth-best debut in franchise history, besting 2015’s second Mockingjay movie ($102.6 million) and 2023 prequel The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ($44.6 million) but behind 2013’s Catching Fire ($158 million), 2012’s series-launching The Hunger Games ($152.5 million) and 2014’s first Mockingjay ($121.8 million). Its $56 million domestic sum on Friday gave Sunrise the third-best debut Friday in franchise history, behind Catching Fire and The Hunger Games.
The new film added $105 million from 84 international territories for a global haul of $225 million.
points: The sixth film in the Lionsgate series rebounded after 2023's 'The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes,' while freshly expanded 'I Play Rocky' and newcomer 'Elsinore' also came out swinging.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson's Divisive Sci-Fi Action Movie Proves He's Perfect For James Bond
articles.summary: Thanks to his role in Christopher Nolan's polarizing sci-fi thriller Tenet, Robert Pattinson has already passed his first test as our new James Bond.
body: How good does Robert Pattinson look in a tailored suit? Damn good, is the answer.

The proof is in Christopher Nolan's 2020 time-warp thriller "Tenet," wherein Pattinson sports a dazzling wardrobe of bespoke suits, knit polos, scarves, and impeccably rumpled pocket squares. The attire in "Tenet," provided by Oscar-nominated costume designer Jeffrey Kurland, are so impressive that GQ Magazine had to pause to write an article about them (even if it was just to complain that the suits look a little too good).
And, as we all know, looking good in a suit is one of the main requirements to play 007, so Pattinson has already passed his first test as our newly-cast James Bond.

However you feel about "Tenet," one has to admit that its costumes are amazing and that Pattinson rocks every single outfit he wears. He carries himself with poise and class, playing the sidekick Neil to the film's protagonist, The Protagonist (John David Washington). Poise and class are the bedrocks on which James Bond is built, and Pattinson can certainly handle those qualities with skill.
points: Thanks to his role in Christopher Nolan's polarizing sci-fi thriller Tenet, Robert Pattinson has already passed his first test as our new James Bond.
